title: Arkret Account Pairing and Agent Operation DTOs
description: Closed request and response DTOs for account pairing and native personal agent management operations.

agent_slug.description: Required controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug. Used only as the right-hand component of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>; not a global handle or authorization subject. Provisioning services MUST issue or update a ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1.

opaque_local_id.description: Deployment-local short-lived account/auth artifact id. It is not a ak:<kind> protocol object id.

pairing_secret.description: One-time CSPRNG pairing secret carrying at least 128 bits of entropy. It is transmitted only in JSON bodies, never in URLs or logs.

device_pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style code carrying 40 CSPRNG bits, bound to a short-lived SAS/QR transcript and protected by a ten-failure lockout.

agent_runtime_key_possession_proof.description: Closed Ed25519 proof that the submitter controls the proposed native Agent runtime key and possesses the authoritative pairing secret. Canonical transcript, equality, freshness, and final-commit re-verification rules are defined in key-management.md section 3.6.2.

audience.description: Stable target-service authorization identity; any verification_method remains a DID URL whose bare full DID MUST project to this did_core_id.

signature.description: Unpadded base64url encoding of the 64-byte raw Ed25519 signature over the canonical transcript.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey DTO. Defined once in public-key.schema.json so device, agent and account surfaces share one definition.

agent_runtime_public_key.description: Closed v1 Native Agent runtime signing-key profile. Ed25519 is the fully-specified JOSE algorithm identifier from RFC 9864; polymorphic algorithm identifiers are rejected.

agent_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent axis. Closed enum; only the controller's pause / resume / deactivate lifecycle events change it. Pairing and key facts are reflected through the generic readiness axis and open-handle fields, never through a fourth generic state axis (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_runtime_state.description: Operation-local diagnostic enum used only by agent_runtime_approval_status_outcome on the unauthenticated pairing poll. It is mechanically derived from the polled handle and key facts, is never writable, and MUST NOT appear in generic Agent list/get/key_state projections: no active accepted key authorization with an unexpired bootstrap handle is pending_runtime_key; no active key with the bootstrap handle expired is pairing_expired; an active key with no unconsumed replacement handle is ready; an active key with an unexpired replacement handle is replacing.

agent_presence.description: Short-lived reachability signal only. It never substitutes for lifecycle or readiness and does not use a protocol-wide fixed five-minute refresh interval.

realm_id.description: Realm that owns the capability grant cell and therefore the required ak.capability.revoke write surface.

key_state.description: Controller-private key, pairing-handle, authorization and PCR-recovery material for a generic Agent view. This object deliberately carries no lifecycle, readiness, presence or runtime_state field: the only three generic status axes are siblings on agent_projection, while pairing poll alone exposes its operation-local runtime_state diagnostic.

requested_scope.description: Controller-private projection of the required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling captured at provision time, not a grant. Content actions are the maximum actions that later key scopes, Realm-scoped grants and sessions may allow; an omitted action cannot be added later. Participation is a separate action-time deny gate and cannot add authority. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants. Receiver authority comes from a valid agent-requested-scope-disclosure whose digest matches the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, not this service projection.

requested_scope_digest.description: sha256 digest of the domain-separated Agent requested_scope commitment fixed in the accepted Agent DID ArkretPrincipalControlRealm service entry; the public entry does not contain the complete scope.

pairing_request_id.description: Current unconsumed, unexpired pairing handle. Its presence means pairing is open. Services MUST omit this field and its pairing_mode / pairing_code / pairing_expires_at siblings immediately after the handle is consumed or expires.

pairing_mode.description: Durable branch discriminator for the current open handle. bootstrap is valid when the Agent has no active accepted runtime-key authorization; replacement is valid when it already holds an active authorized key and lifecycle is active or paused. This field is pairing material, not a fourth generic status axis.

pairing_expires_at.description: Authoritative pairing expiry instant in the shared byte-canonical UTC millisecond profile. The projection and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1.expires_at use the same exact string; offset or sub-millisecond wire spellings are schema violations and MUST NOT be normalized by a verifier.

agent_pcr_recovery_state.description: Controller-visible recovery readiness for the managed Agent Principal Control Realm. pending means no accepted controller-owned managed-PCR backup exists; ready means the current controller recovery policy and Agent PCR sealed MLS frontier are covered by the active mls_history series tail; stale means an older backup exists but no longer covers the current policy, delegation, Seal frontier, or MLS epoch. Runtime pairing commits require ready at the pre-commit frontier; the accepted key-authorization Event then advances the frontier and makes this projection stale until a post-commit backup tail is accepted.

challenge_proof.description: Structured proof of possession of new_device_pubkey. The Account Authority MUST recompute the signing transcript itself and MUST NOT settle for byte equality against a stored copy. Which transcript applies is fixed by the request shape: with device_pairing_request_id it is ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 rebuilt from the staged record; with challenge_transcript it is ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 rebuilt from those inputs plus the Account Authority own gate_audience origin. The digest of that recomputed transcript is also the value the target device_signature commits to, so one recomputation gates both proofs. A mismatched transcript_digest, a transcript name that does not match the request shape, a kid other than new_device_pubkey.kid, or a failing signature MUST NOT authorize a device.

hpke_key.description: New target device X25519 HPKE public key. It MUST be byte-identical to authorize_event.event.payload.hpke_key and is never generated or substituted by the service. Its authority is the out-of-band device_pairing_target_attestation the approving device verified, not the staged record: the unauthenticated staging surface never carries this value.

device_signature.description: Target-device Ed25519 possession proof over ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1: this operation always produces authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, so registration_anchor and pcr_recovery possession domains MUST be rejected here. It MUST be byte-identical to authorize_event.event.payload.device_signature and verify under new_device_pubkey.

authorize_event.description: Fully signed ak.device.authorize initial submission authored by a current accepted device. The service MUST admit this exact Event through the ordinary Event validation/reducer path; it MUST NOT mint an Event id, rewrite the Event, or directly insert a device projection. The payload MUST name the target new_device_pubkey.kid, hpke_key and device_signature from this request, set authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, and name the approving current device id in authorized_by. The proof.verification_method bare DID component MUST project through its registered adapter to principal_id and its fragment MUST equal authorized_by; appending a fragment to did_core_id is forbidden. That Event proof, not the target device_signature, binds principal_id, authorized_by, not_before, expires_at and scopes, because only the approving device knows those values.

device_pairing_request_id.description: Server-mediated short-link request id. Present exactly for the short-link path. The Account Authority MUST atomically authorize only the still-pending staged record whose pairing_code and new_device_pubkey exactly match this request, and MUST verify challenge_proof against the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript rebuilt from that record (device_pairing_request_id, pairing_code, gate_audience, expires_at, server_nonce, client_nonce, new_device_pubkey digest). A record whose proof does not verify MUST NOT authorize a device.

challenge_transcript.description: Transcript inputs for the to-device path, where there is no staged record for the Account Authority to rebuild from. Present exactly when device_pairing_request_id is absent.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Controller-signed private disclosure addressed to the authoritative pairing verifier. The endpoint MUST consume its presentation challenge once, match agent/controller/audience, recompute the public DID commitment digest, and use the disclosed scope for the subset check. It MUST NOT copy the disclosure into authorize_event or any durable/public history.

signing_key_binding.description: Controller-signed minimal public binding created in the same approval action. Its agent/method/raw-key/authorization id and both digests MUST match the runtime request and authorize_event exactly.

authorize_event.description: Fully-signed ak.agent.key.authorize initial submission approved by the controller or policy engine. Its Event MUST target the Agent Principal Control Realm, carry actor_id equal to agent_id, executed_by equal to the controller DID, authorization_ref equal to the controller delegation DID URL bound by the Agent DID Document, and a proof verification method belonging to the controller or one of its currently authorized devices. The submission MUST carry ordinary publication authority evidence without rewriting the Event. Its payload.agent_key_scope MAY be narrower than, but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of, the immutable provision requested_scope; every provision constraint remains mandatory. Required so key activation never depends on an unaudited pairing side effect. authorize_event.event.event_id is the pair operation idempotency identity.

activation_state.description: Two-phase pairing result. awaiting_accepted_frontier means the exact authorization Event is durable but is not yet authorization state; the controller MUST close it into a managed Agent-PCR Seal and retry the identical idempotent request. active means portable signer evidence can be built from an accepted Seal and only then may the runtime be treated as authorized.

agent_runtime_approval_request_body.description: Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The runtime proves possession of the local key and the short pairing code; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize and submitting agent_key_pair_request_body. The service computes ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 from agent_id, pairing_request_id, verification_method, public-key digest and attestation digest. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable binding: same-binding retry is idempotent and refreshes the full request while retaining approval/notification ids; a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_controller_projec.description: Authenticated controller-safe projection of the pending runtime key request. It is deliberately not agent_runtime_approval_request_body and not agent_key_pair_request_body: pairing_code is exposed only by the sibling controller key_state field, while requested_scope_disclosure and authorize_event do not exist until the controller approves. Services MUST also omit any other runtime secret or unregistered field.

agent_human_approval_error_details.description: Closed error.details shape returned by ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant when an agent_key_proof request needs out-of-band controller approval. The enclosing ErrorEnvelope.error.code MUST be claim_required. The agent runtime MUST NOT be given CAPTCHA, OTP, browser-login, or other interactive human challenge material.

agent_runtime_approval_status_request_bo.description: Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id, pairing_code, and agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. A record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and stop polling after pairing expiry.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_status_outcome.description: Controller-decision status for one runtime key pairing request. runtime_state is an operation-specific pairing diagnostic, not a fourth general Agent status axis. While the polled pairing is open it is pending_runtime_key (bootstrap) or replacing (replacement). Once the controller has approved this exact pairing, authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding fields are present; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key. Presence and digest match of those fields — never lifecycle, readiness, presence or runtime_state alone — is the approval signal. An expired bootstrap reports pairing_expired; an expired replacement reports ready with no authorization fields for this request.

authorized_public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decoded 32-byte Ed25519 public key, computed with agent_signing_public_key_digest. This is not the canonical runtime-request PublicKey DTO digest.

agent_provision_request_body.description: Controller-authored managed-Agent bootstrap. Before prepare, the controller publishes a signed, PCR-independent did:webvh inception whose document contains the managed-controller delegation but no ArkretPrincipalControlRealm service. prepare receives that full_id, verifies the accepted inception and returns its exact initial_resolution plus an opaque allocation. The controller freezes the managed-Agent PCR genesis with that commitment, derives principal_control_realm_id, and commits one ak.agent.provision Event. After PCR acceptance, the controller publishes the pre-rotation-authorized DID update containing the create-locked Realm binding. The service exposes the Agent and pairing handle only after that update is accepted.

full_id.description: Controller-authored Agent did:webvh whose accepted inception is independent of the future PCR Realm id.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id the controller derived as retype(event_id) of the managed Agent PCR ak.realm.create envelope it froze locally, and signed into provision_event. A service MUST NOT choose it; commit MUST reject any value that differs from the provision payload byte for byte. It is distinct from the controller PCR that carries provision_event. This transport field is not inside any digest preimage; the ordering the controller MUST follow is key-management.md 3.6.3 and the named encoding.md 6.0.1 exemption on the payload field.

requested_scope.description: Required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling, not a grant. Later key scopes, Realm grants and session requests MUST NOT exceed its actions, resource selectors or mandatory constraints. Participation is an independent action-time deny gate and cannot restore authority omitted here. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants.

controller_principal_server_id.description: Authenticated controller account Principal Server. Together with the session principal_id this selects the controller authority; PCR identifiers are not exposed.

agent_provision_outcome.description: Four-stage outcome. prepare returns awaiting_controller_event with an accepted inception commitment. An accepted ak.agent.provision moves it to awaiting_pcr_genesis. PCR acceptance moves it to awaiting_did_binding until the controller-authored continuous WebVH update publishes the exact Realm service entry. The Agent, pairing handle and list/get projection become visible only at complete.

full_id.description: Complete Agent DID whose registered adapter projection is agent_id; managed-Agent PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST commit this value and its verified method head.

initial_resolution.description: Exact verified accepted inception position. It is immutable across all provisioning outcomes and is copied byte-for-byte into managed-Agent PCR genesis.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id the controller derived locally as retype(event_id) of the managed Agent PCR genesis it froze, and declared in the provision payload. Until that genesis is accepted this is a claim, not a live Realm.

controller_realm_id.description: Authenticated controller PCR in which the provision Event must be authored. Present only while status is awaiting_controller_event.

allocation_handle.description: Service-signed opaque allocation binding returned only by prepare and presented unchanged by commit.

requested_scope_digest.description: Digest of the complete immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID accepted create-locked bootstrap history (entry 1); only this digest, not the complete scope, is public. The client MUST recompute it from its submitted scope, returned agent_id and authenticated controller DID.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_challenge.description: Request the single-use challenge that makes abandoning an accepted-but-never-genesised Agent provisioning explicit. It applies only while ak.agent.provision is accepted and the declared managed Agent PCR genesis has not been accepted, so the Agent has no PCR, no DID service entry, no pairing handle and no list/get projection. agent_id, principal_control_realm_id and allocation_handle pin exactly which provisioning is being given up.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Realm id the accepted provision declared. The service MUST reject any other value and MUST NOT issue a challenge once the genesis for it is accepted.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_consequen.description: Closed ordered set of consequences the client MUST present before it may submit the confirmation. The protocol fixes which consequences must be disclosed; the localized wording is deployment-owned. It is not a self-asserted acknowledgement receipt, which would be forgeable; the anti-automation property comes from the challenge itself, which no ordinary flow ever fetches.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_challenge.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for abandoning an Agent provisioning whose PCR genesis never arrived. It is the evidence that the abandonment was an explicit controller action. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

expires_at.description: MUST be at most 300 seconds after issued_at.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_request_b.description: Confirm the explicit abandonment of an Agent provisioning whose PCR genesis never arrived. It MUST present fresh credentials and MUST NOT reuse the ones presented when the challenge was issued; how strong that re-authentication is, which risk checks run and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified here.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the abandonment. Replaying it returns the recorded terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone.

agent_provisioning_abandonment_outcome.description: Recorded terminal outcome of an explicit provisioning abandonment. One transaction consumed the challenge, released the agent_slug selector claim and the principal_control_realm_id claim, recorded the tombstone / audit reservation and suppressed every holder-readable trace of the allocation. There is exactly one success terminal; every other terminal is an error reply. The accepted ak.agent.provision Event itself stays in the controller PCR history and is never deleted or rewritten.

principal_control_realm_id.description: The abandoned realm-id claim. It MUST NOT be reused by a later provision, and no Realm will ever exist at it.

agent_renew_pairing_request_body.description: Re-open bootstrap pairing or replace an agent runtime. The service issues a fresh one-time pairing_request_id + pairing_code; every previously issued pairing handle for the agent becomes permanently unresolvable. An Agent with no active accepted runtime-key authorization re-opens bootstrap pairing; an Agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle active or paused) performs runtime replacement re-pairing. Lifecycle intent, existing keys and grants stay untouched until the new controller-signed authorization with an exact supersedes set is accepted atomically, and completion preserves lifecycle intent. deactivated rejects.

agent_renew_pairing_outcome.description: Fresh pairing handle plus the current managed Agent PCR recovery projection. Unlike initial provisioning, pcr_recovery can already be ready or stale; pair commit still requires ready.

requested_scope_digest.description: Unchanged digest of the immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID binding; the complete scope remains controller-private.

agent_pairing_bootstrap.description: One-time bootstrap material handed to a personal agent runtime after provisioning. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret.

agent_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for short agent pairing handoff links. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.self.agent.pause Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. The service submits these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and never synthesizes an Agent-authored Event. Its optional payload.reason MUST equal the request reason exactly (both absent or the same string).

Closed ak.self.agent.resume Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. Sidecar desired membership is re-derived from accepted lifecycle and exact Realm membership after admission; the request carries no writable Sidecar roster or acknowledgement.

The single controller-authorized terminal ak.self.agent.deactivate Event. Once accepted, lifecycle is an unavoidable AND gate that makes every subordinate runtime key, session, pairing handle, capability grant, KeyPackage, presence and future submission ineffective. Cleanup Events are not part of this request. Optional payload.reason MUST equal request reason.

grant_event.description: Complete controller-authored ak.capability.grant initial submission. event.payload.grant is a closed CapabilityGrantBody without an inner proof; the Event envelope proof is the sole durable issuer signature. Admission MUST verify that event.actor_id, event.realm_id, payload.grant_id, grant.id, grant.issuer, grant.subject and grant.realm_id match the authenticated controller, path Agent and governed Realm as applicable. Every action and resource must be covered by the requested_scope disclosed in the verifier-bound private sidecar, and provision constraints remain mandatory. A violation fails with agent_grant_exceeds_requested_scope. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT synthesize the Event or fall back to a body-local signature.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Fresh, controller-signed private ceiling disclosure addressed to the grant admission verifier. It is transaction evidence only and MUST NOT be copied into the Realm-scoped grant or Event history.

agent_grant_detach_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.capability.revoke Control Move and nothing else. The path grant_id MUST equal payload.grant_id and optional payload.grant_ref; the target grant subject MUST equal the path Agent; event.realm_id MUST equal the target grant Realm. The service submits the exact signed Event through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT rebuild it, synthesize a revoke Event, or attach a precondition after signing.

revoke_event.description: Complete controller-authored ak.capability.revoke initial submission. The Event MUST carry exactly one signed head_eq precondition on ak:cell:ak.component.capability.grant.v1:<payload.grant_id>, naming the complete observed grant-cell head. event.actor_id is the authenticated controller and admission binds its proof to the session-selected exact account-local lineage. Ordinary capability target guards remain authoritative: only the target issuer or current root controller of the target grant Realm may revoke it. Exact replay is idempotent; stale CAS, unsigned requests, and same-Event-ID different-body attempts fail closed.

agent_sidecar_context_ref.description: Existing shared Strand or Relation used only as the UI/source context for a native Sidecar projection. It does not create or identify a private Strand.

control_frontier.description: UTF-8 byte-lexicographically sorted accepted refs for Sidecar genesis, ownership, Agent lifecycle/runtime-key authorization, and exact Realm membership. It excludes action grants, participation selections, and MLS/key-readiness results.

current_controller_device_ready.description: True only when the authenticated controller session device is the accepted genesis creator device or has completed matching Welcome and KeyPackage consume evidence.

desired_agent_ids.description: Read-only projection derived at the accepted frontier: active, runtime-key-authorized Agent principals owned by the Sidecar controller and also active members of sidecar.realm_id. It is not caller-authored or reducer-stored and cannot be edited through Sidecar operations.

effective_agent_ids.description: Desired Agent principals that are members of the current accepted Sidecar MLS epoch and have completed target-device Welcome/KeyPackage consumption and key readiness. Reducer/service MUST enforce this set is a subset of desired_agent_ids. The controller is represented by sidecar.controller_id and is not duplicated in either Agent array.

version.description: Account Authority CAS version for this exact agent/scope selection.

expected_version.description: Value to echo verbatim into the next participation replace for this exact agent/scope selection.

next_replace_input.description: Verbatim prepare input for the next ak.self.agent.participation.resource.replace of this entry; member names match the replace request byte-for-byte per the service-http-binding.md 2.2.2 echo-container discipline. A first-ever selection has no entry row and uses expected_version 0.
